EMPLOYER IS A CONTRACTOR FOR THE U.S. GOVERNMENT. THIS POSITION REQUIRES U.S. CITIZENSHIP.

Role Description

This is a forward-deployed engineering role. You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with mission heroes- the users, operators, and program engineers who run real workloads in real DoD environments- and lead the software integration of modular Counter-Unmanned Aerial Systems (C-UAS) sensors and effectors. You will deploy, harden, integrate, and operate our modular C-UAS solution.

Forward-deployed means aligned with the mission hero, not always on a plane. Most of the work is remote. You'll travel to sites when the engagement genuinely calls for it — initial standup, in-SCIF integration work, on-the-ground incident response, training, and knowledge transfer- and you'll be on a video call or in a shared chat with that same mission hero the rest of the time. The job is being their engineer, not living at their desk.

You are a cross-functional engineering leader. You can take responsibility for the full breadth of a data and software integration platform- make it work where it has to work, analyze what's running through it, and solve problems in real time for the mission hero. About 20% of your time, you'll also help make Defense Unicorns' forward-deployed team better — pairing with junior Data Engineer FDEs on hard problems, helping them develop technical judgment, and raising the ceiling on what the team can take on.

Responsibilities

  • Deploy and harden UDS Data Capability in the mission hero's environment — stand up UDS Store (Iceberg, Rook/Ceph, pgvector, Postgres), wire up UDS Transit for air-gap data movement, configure UDS Govern policies (Pepr/Lula), and integrate UDS Connect (Strimzi/Kafka) where streaming or legacy connectors are required.

  • Own integration with existing mission systems — connect UDS Data Capability to existing infrastructure, including sensor arrays, computer-vision-enabled UAS interceptors, and a broad range of C-UAS solutions.

  • Build pipelines that move data through classification boundaries — ingestion, transformation, catalog registration, model/dataset packaging via Zarf, cross-domain transit, and eventual consistency across DDIL conditions.

  • Operate what you deploy — own initial day-2 operations, including capacity, performance, backup/restore (Velero), observability (Vector/Loki), incident response, and upgrade paths. Transition ownership to the mission hero's operations team once stable.

  • Generate accreditation artifacts — STIG evidence, cATO documentation, FIPS validation notes, and policy mappings to support ISSM/ISSO requirements in IL4/IL5 environments.

  • Represent the mission hero to product and engineering — document issues, write postmortems, recommend operator improvements, and communicate field challenges to the platform engineering team.

  • Train and transfer knowledge — develop runbooks, architecture documentation, working sessions, and knowledge-transfer materials that enable mission teams to operate independently.

  • Mentor junior Data Engineer FDEs — pair on complex problems, review integration designs, and help engineers develop technical judgment without direct people-management responsibilities.

Clearance & Travel

  • Clearance: Active TS/SCI required.

  • Travel: Approximately 10%–25%, based on mission and customer requirements.

  • On-site expectations: Ability to work in SCIFs and other restricted environments for days or weeks when required for integration, incident response, training, or knowledge transfer. Most work is performed remotely.

  • Research and apply emerging practices in AI-assisted vulnerability remediation, including prompt engineering, context engineering, and vulnerability-specific fix guidance.

  • Identify which vulnerability types are suitable for automated remediation, balancing security impact, technical feasibility, and developer experience.

  • Collaborate with developers and security stakeholders to collect feedback through code reviews, pull requests, support channels, and interactive sessions, using these insights to improve remediation quality.

  • Help shape how Spotify approaches security posture management by building scalable solutions that reduce security risks and make it easier for teams to address vulnerabilities.

Role Description

Compliance Lead decides what the systems must satisfy, can configure the controls personally in Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 GCC High, writes the record that proves it, and verifies the result the way an assessor would.

This is not a coordination role. The Compliance Lead scopes the assessment boundary, authors the System Security Plan and supporting documentation, directs and where needed performs control implementation, assesses the finished environment against the CMMC Level 2 Assessment Guide, and stands next to the customer during the assessment. They are the day-to-day point of contact for their assigned customers and answer CMMC questions with authority and in plain terms. Customer environments vary: Windows and macOS fleets, GCC High and Google Workspace tenants, Jamf and Intune, cloud and on-prem enclaves. This person has to be versatile enough to work in all of them.

The listed responsibilities are not exhaustive and additional responsibilities may be assigned based on the evolving needs of the organization. We are seeking a dynamic individual who is able to adapt and take on new responsibilities as they arise.

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned customers for the life of the engagement: run kickoff, working sessions, and status reporting; answer CMMC and NIST SP 800-171 questions directly and accurately without escalation.
  • Scope the CMMC assessment boundary: trace FCI and CUI flows, categorize assets per the CMMC Level 2 Scoping Guide (CUI, Security Protection, Contractor Risk Managed, Specialized, Out of Scope), and produce the boundary, data-flow, and network diagrams.
  • Lead each engagement through the standard delivery process from intake to assessor-ready package, holding the stage gates and evidence standards.
  • Author and maintain the System Security Plan, policies and procedures, POA&M, and evidence library at the assessment-objective level; score self-assessments and SPRS submissions under the DoD Assessment Methodology and 32 CFR Part 170.
  • Implement the technical controls hands-on in the customer tenant: identity, MFA, and conditional access in Entra ID or Google Cloud Identity; least privilege and privileged-account separation; data protection in Microsoft Purview or Google Workspace DLP; FIPS-validated encryption; configuration baselines. Decide which requirement each setting satisfies and why, and split the heavier build work with the Technical Implementation Engineer.
  • Stand up and operate endpoint management across Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android with Microsoft Intune and Jamf (Apple Business Manager, Android Enterprise): enrollment, compliance policies, CIS or DISA STIG baselines, BitLocker and FileVault, patching, and removable-media control.
  • Build the logging and monitoring stack the AU, RA, and SI practices require: centralized audit logging and alerting in a SIEM (Microsoft Sentinel, Google SecOps, Splunk, or similar), log retention and review cadence, vulnerability scanning and remediation tracking, and backup and recovery verification.
  • Assess the finished environment against the CMMC Level 2 Assessment Guide using examine, interview, and test methods; run the pre-assessment readiness review and close gaps before the C3PAO arrives.
  • Prepare customers for C3PAO assessments and support them during assessment week: evidence presentation, interview coaching, assessor questions, and post-assessment POA&M closeout.
  • Run sustainment for customers: continuous monitoring cadence, change reviews, annual affirmations, and reassessment readiness.
  • Improve the practice: turn repeatable work into templates, checklists, and automation, and contribute domain content to the team's internal AI tooling.

  • Hands-on experience implementing NIST SP 800-171 technical controls yourself in Microsoft 365 GCC High (Entra ID, Intune, Purview, Defender) or Google Workspace (Admin console, Cloud Identity, context-aware access, endpoint management): the admin-console work, not only the policy; able to validate what an implementation engineer built rather than accept a screenshot.
  • Endpoint management experience across Windows and macOS (iOS and Android a plus) with at least one of Microsoft Intune or Jamf: enrollment, compliance and configuration policies, disk encryption, patching, and hardening baselines.
  • Experience centralizing audit logs and alerts in a SIEM or log platform (Microsoft Sentinel, Google SecOps, Splunk, or similar) and operating vulnerability scanning, patch management, and backup to satisfy the AU, RA, SI, and MP practices.
  • Working knowledge of networking and perimeter controls (firewalls, VPN and secure remote access, segmentation, DNS, wireless), enough to scope the boundary and verify the SC practices.
  • Customer-facing lead: runs meetings, explains requirements in plain terms to executives and IT staff, documents decisions, pushes back constructively, and delivers without close supervision.
  • Ability to run multiple concurrent engagements (typically 4–6), track milestones, and report status in a remote, asynchronous environment (Slack, Notion, Google Workspace).

Preferred Experience and Qualifications

  • CMMC Certified Assessor (CCA) strongly preferred; CMMC Certified Professional (CCP) at minimum. Lead CCA designation or Registered Practitioner Advanced (RPA) a plus.
  • Hands-on implementation experience in both Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 GCC High, including GCC High migrations and Google Workspace configurations built to NIST SP 800-171.
  • Depth in Apple Business Manager, Android Enterprise, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Sentinel, or Google SecOps; CIS Benchmarks or DISA STIG hardening; Windows Server and Active Directory in hybrid environments.
  • CUI enclave design and migration: GCC High, Azure Government, AWS GovCloud, or on-prem enclaves, including FedRAMP Moderate equivalency evaluation of cloud service providers and scoping of external service providers.
